findings.title: `sq stats reviews --json` emits plain text when the review directory is missing
findings.description: `stats_reviews` checks `report.missing_dir` before the `as_json` branch. It prints `No review directory at ...` to stdout and returns with exit 0, even under `--json`. A script that pipes `--json` output into a JSON parser will fail on this path. Emit a valid JSON document for the missing-directory case, with `missing_dir: true` and empty rows. Or print the message to stderr when `--json` is set. The test `test_reviews_missing_dir_exits_0_with_message` only covers the table mode.

findings.title: A review provider failure is now returned as a result instead of re-raised
findings.description: `_review_part` used to re-raise `ProviderError` after saving the failure artifact, so it reached `execute`'s catch-all. It now returns `self._exception_result(...)` directly. I could not check whether callers of `_review_part` (the split and gated multi-part paths, `_gated_parts`) inspect `success` on the returned part. If they only expect exceptions for failures, a failed part could be treated as a normal part. The log call also uses `_logger.exception("review: unexpected error ...")` for a named `ProviderError`. The dispatch path logs named provider failures as a single ERROR line without a traceback (issue 200), so the two paths are now inconsistent. The wording "unexpected" is misleading for a named failure. Confirm the callers handle a failed part result, and add a test for a multi-part review where one part fails.

findings.title: `except ProviderError` is placed ahead of the other specific handlers in `DispatchAction.execute`
findings.description: The diff moves `except ProviderError` above `except (ModelResolutionError, ModelPoolNotImplemented, KeyError)` and the handlers below it. If any of those exception types, or `ContextForgeError` or `ProjectRulesError`, subclasses `ProviderError`, it would now be routed to `_provider_failure` and lose its specific handling. I could not verify the class hierarchy. Check the hierarchy and add a test that each specific handler is still reached.

findings.title: `UsageCapture.effort_for_session` has a side effect and a constant return value
findings.description: The method is named like a getter and always returns `None`. Its real work is logging a DEBUG message once, via a mutable flag. Callers write `effort_sent = capture.effort_for_session(resolved)`, which reads as if the effort varies. Split it into a logging method such as `note_session_effort_gap`, and pass `None` explicitly as the sent effort.

findings.title: Overly broad exception tuple used to absorb a malformed top-level value
findings.description: `except (OSError, ValueError, AttributeError, SchemaVersionError)` catches `AttributeError` to cover a state file whose top-level JSON value is not an object. Catching `AttributeError` can hide real programming errors inside `StateManager.load` and report them as "cannot read file". Validate the shape inside `StateManager.load`, or raise a specific error there.

findings.title: Pricing-warning dedupe is lost on the review path
findings.description: `run_review_with_profile` calls `resolve_cost(..., set())` with a fresh set each time. The pipeline path deduplicates via the run's `UsageCapture`, but standalone reviews and split-review parts warn on every call. Consider accepting an optional shared warning set.

findings.title: Large positional parameter plumbing
findings.description: `usage_capture` is threaded through about ten `_execute_*` functions, which take `Any`-typed collaborators. This follows the existing pattern, but each new run-scoped collaborator widens every signature. Consider bundling the run-scoped collaborators into one object later.

findings.title: Test coverage for the new reporting and capture code is good
findings.description: The tests cover partial records, malformed usage, pre-slice run files, cancellation propagation, and the missing-capture error. They use a real captured `ResultMessage` fixture, which fits the parser-fixture rule in CLAUDE.md. The one gap is the `--json` missing-directory case noted above.
